subject: Next steps: Voxenta POC acceptance matrix & model fallback
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@voxenta.com>, Tom Hirst <tom.h@voxenta.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Voxenta POC acceptance matrix & model fallback

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed plan so we have clear next steps heading into the POC kickoff: 

Summary of ask
- Use Redwood inference to power Voxenta’s chat summarization and customer intent routing for English and Spanish traffic.
- Success = automated summaries that match or exceed your current baseline (human scoring) + routing accuracy >= 92% for top-2 intents.

Proposed POC scope (4 weeks) — high level
1) Week 0 (this week): agree acceptance matrix, share sample dataset (500 de-identified chats), and confirm security checklist.
2) Week 1: baseline run on two candidate open models + collect metrics (latency, token cost, quality).
3) Week 2: iterate prompts and fallback rules; enable prefix/KV caching for throughput tests.
4) Week 3: acceptance evaluation (automated metrics + 10 human spot-checks); compile results and decide on go/no-go.

Model plan (initial recommendation)
- Primary: Mistral-7B-Instruct (q8) — strong English performance, fast p50 latency on our Dedicated pools.
- Fallback (especially for Spanish & edge cases): Llama2-Chat-13B (q4) — better multilingual handling in our tests and higher robustness to noisy transcripts.
- If cost becomes a blocker we will try RedPajama-INCITE-3B as an ultra-low-cost fallback for non-critical summarization tasks.

Acceptance matrix (we’ll attach a template) — key signals
- Quality: automated F1 on annotated intents, human rating >= 4/5 on summaries (10 blind samples).
- Latency: p50 < 220ms and p95 < 600ms on Dedicated pool at expected load (50 rps).
- Cost: token cost not to exceed $0.035 per conversation on average (estimate).
- Reliability: <1% error rate, graceful fallback path if primary model returns malformed output.

Ownership
- Logan (me): engagement lead, timelines, and primary contact for Voxenta.
- Marissa Cole: evaluation owner — designs rubric, runs human checks, consolidates results.
- Karthik Iyer: infra/model mapping — sets model quantization/profile on Dedicated, configures autoscaling.

Attachments: Voxenta-POC-Acceptance-Matrix.xlsx (draft) and sample_prompts_spanish_en.jsonl — please review.

Alyssa — can you confirm: 1) the dataset drop timeline (you mentioned end of this week), and 2) if procurement needs a SOW for kickoff?

If that all looks good we’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Monday to get credentials and dataset access.

Thanks,
Logan

--
Logan Wright

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the dataset: we can anonymize and upload 500 chat transcripts by Friday 2026-09-04 EOD in the S3 bucket you shared (I’ll invite procurement to the SOW thread separately).

A couple of quick notes:
- Spanish coverage is critical for our LATAM region. We’d like the fallback logic to be explicit (e.g., language-detection -> if Spanish then prefer Llama2, else Mistral).
- For acceptance, the human review group will be 5 people (mix of CS and QA). We’ll share the rubric with Marissa once she’s looped in.

Yes to kickoff Monday — propose 9:00am PT.

Best,
Alyssa

alyssa@voxenta.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Voxenta POC acceptance matrix & model fallback

Thanks both — I uploaded the draft acceptance matrix to the Drive link Logan shared and attached an xlsx here for quick review. High-level changes I made:

- Split quality checks into Intents (automated F1) and Summaries (human rating).
- Added sample-size and statistical confidence (we’ll use 500 conversations with 10 human spot-checks).
- Specified fallback mechanics: 1) language detect -> use Llama2-Chat-13B for Spanish, 2) if primary model fails schema validation -> route to fallback with a per-request circuit breaker.

Example evaluation rubric (excerpt)
- Summary fidelity (human): 1–5 scale; pass if mean >= 4.0 and no sample < 3.
- Intent precision: top-1 precision >= 88%, top-2 recall >= 92%.
- Latency: p50 <= 220ms (Dedicated) and p95 <= 600ms.

Open questions for Voxenta:
- Will the human reviewers use the same UI as current CS agents or do you want our evaluation harness (we can provide a simple labeling UI)?
- Do you expect simultaneous evaluation across EN/ES or staged? Staging lets us iterate faster on English prompts before Spanish validation.

Next steps I’ll take this afternoon:
- Lock the test harness and share credentials to the Voxenta reviewers.
- Prepare baseline runs on the two candidate models and send initial metric table by Friday.

Logan — can you set the kickoff for Monday 9:00am PT and include the S3 access steps?

Thanks,
Marissa
